The binding now passes `--extra anthropic` to `uv sync --locked`. This means the provision step installs the anthropic SDK into the repository's own environment unconditionally, not just when the job needs it. Adopters whose bindings mirror this file will pull in the anthropic SDK on every provision. The comment explains why (provision runs from the base branch and could otherwise uninstall what the job installed), which is the correct reasoning — but the side effect is worth naming: this is now…[truncated]

The `recorded` call wraps `invoker.provider` in place by assignment after the factory returns. This relies on `invoker` having a mutable `provider` attribute. If an adapter's factory returns an invoker whose `provider` is a property with no setter, the assignment silently fails in Python (or raises, depending on implementation). The diff does not show `AiInvoker`'s definition, so I cannot confirm whether this is safe — but the pattern is fragile if `provider` is ever made read-only.
